My husband had just come back from London late at night after a long and difficult journey, where he picked me up in Salisbury before taking me to Portsmouth for work. It was an inconvenient trip for him, especially with road closures, and he still had another drive back to Winchester ahead of him, where he had to wake up early for work the next day.

When I realized I had forgotten my phone charger, I texted him to bring me one. However, he didn’t have one in the car and would have had to go back to work, grab the charger, and then come back to deliver it before returning to Winchester. He offered to bring it the next evening after work instead, pointing out that I still had my iPad and that he could contact me through my landlady if there was an emergency. He also says he had politely reminded me multiple times to charge my phone and even asked if I had everything before we left the house. 

However, this time, he decided to "teach me a lesson" by not bringing the charger immediately, intending to reinforce that I need to be more responsible with my phone. I became very upset and told him how serious the situation was to me, even threatening to divorce him over it.

AITA for insisting my husband drop everything and bring me a phone charger that night?

AITA for blowing up at my in laws and wife over them trying to ruin our vacation plans? My wife and I have 2 kids (4f & 2f). We moved to another country about a year ago and have been living here ever since. When in our home country, both families were very involved in our lives due to my kids being the only grandchildren on both sides. Us moving overseas caused my in laws to feel as if we were abandoning them and they will lose the bond they have with their grandkids and we only doing it for the money and not thinking about them. So we agreed during summers we will send the kids back home for about 6 weeks to spend time with both grandparents.

In September my wife and I explored the idea of going for a vacation without the kids to reconnect and be a couple again. We discussed and she agreed that it will be good for us. We then speak to my inlaws and explain to them when and why we want to go for our solo holiday. They were very excited at the prospect of spending time with the kids so all seemed well. Now, knowing that my in laws can be very reactionary people I told them to think about it and we will discuss again in a few days time. We call them 3 days later and discuss and they of the same mindset. As i said i know how reactionary they can be so i brought it up with them every 2 or 3 days  for about a month which is ALOT of discussion around the same subject. I wanted to make sure all is fine. This is what we agreed to:

1. Wife and kids will fly home late December to leave the kids and to get the kids used to the grand parents again and vice versa
2. Wife will return late Jan so she can spend some time here and do some things she wanted to do without having to worry about the kids
3. Early Feb wife and I will depart for Bali after which we will go to home country to spend some time
4. So in total, we will be leaving the kids in their care for 4 weeks

On Monday my in laws ask her if she is serious about leaving the kids for so long and that they are worried that the kids won't manage and she must push her flight later so the kids only spend the minimum amount of time without us - they want her to fly back only a day or two before we leave for vacation as opposed to the 2 weeks that has been planned and paid for. She called me on Monday night to talk to me about it and said that she AGREES with them I. Lost. My. Shit. I demanded a conference call with her parents straight away and basically let them have it for emotionally manipulating my wife. I said if they try and demand this I will take my kids with us to Bali and they can forget about us ever leaving the kids with them again and I will not be sending them down over the summers. I said I will not ask them for anything ever again and called them assholes for not keeping to the agreement even though we discussed it more than 20 times.I told my wife this is bullshit as she was fine with the arrangements whenever we discussed it. I said she needs to grow a spine and stick to her decision.

AITA?

My 21F best friend “K” had a birthday party back in 2019. Days before her party she asked me and our other best friend “A” for money since she haven’t gotten her birthday gift from her parents (which is the money she will use to pay for the expenses for her party). She told us she would pay me and A as soon as she got her money so me and A chipped in to pay for her party. 3 years later, she still hasn’t paid us back. There were multiple times when me and A asked her if she can pay us back. But each time we ask her, she will just apologize, tell us she doesn’t have any money at the moment, and promise that she will pay us back once she have money. 

But it has been 3 years already. We went out countless of times already but she never paid us back. I don’t know if she forgot she owes us money but It’s just awkward to keep asking her to pay when it should’ve have been her responsibility to pay us back even if we don’t ask. Now I’m thinking of asking her again to pay me back because I desperately need the money but I am too shy to ask. Should I just forget that she owes us money or should I still ask her to pay? I desperately need money right now and the only way I can think of is to get that money back. What should I do?

TL;DR
My best friend borrowed money from me 3 years ago and she still hasn’t paid me back. I need money right now and am thinking to ask her to pay me back. Should I still ask her or should I just forget she owes me money because it has been 2 years already?

Update: Sorry for the late update. I got caught up with school and family stuff but thank you all for showing concern in my personal matter. I didn’t expect for this post to blow up. I saw most of the comments saying that I shouldn’t lend money and expect it to come back. I get this know. But here in my country, we have this thinking that it is much safer to lend money to our family and friends (if they need it) since they are closer to us and they are the ones who we trust more in paying us back our money. Well I learned the hard way that even your best friend you can’t trust 100%. And if you guys are wondering if I talked to her or what, I didn’t. You guys are right, the money is gone. What I will do is to never lend her or anyone anything ever again. I think if ever I will loan anybody again is if only they badly need it (eg. medical bills, any emergency stuff, etc). Anyway, thank you so much again you guys for taking time to make me realize things. Hope all are well.

AITA for having high expectations for my (M50s) employees, including my son?  

Last year, my son (M26) came to me after losing his retail job. He was feeling uncertain and looking for work, and since I run a small local business, I offered him a position. I thought it would also give us a chance to reconnect, as our relationship has been somewhat distant over the years.  

I admit I have high standards for my business. It's my livelihood, and I’ve worked hard to build it. I expect my employees to meet those standards – including my son. Over the years, I’ve developed ways of handling situations that work for me, and sometimes I may come across as dismissive or direct in how I address issues. But in my mind, that's just what’s needed to keep things running.  

While he was working here, my son seemed to have difficulty adjusting to the pace and structure of the job. For example, when he brought up that our water boiler wasn’t working properly, I didn’t initially see it as a big issue, because it seemed like it was functioning well enough at the time. Things like this happen in a fast-paced work environment, and I didn’t think it required immediate attention. I’ll admit, I might have overlooked his concerns too quickly – but I was trying to focus on bigger priorities.  

When mistakes happened, I did address them directly, which seemed to upset him. There were also times he brought me feedback from other staff, but I didn’t always agree with his points. To me, some of the struggles he described are just part and parcel of running a small business.  

The breaking point seems to have been when I shared constructive criticism after we received a negative review. I pointed out where I believed his performance could have been improved. I wasn’t trying to be harsh, but to highlight areas where expectations weren’t met and where things could've been done differently. However, he took it very personally, argued back, and then walked out mid-shift after telling me I was being "unrealistic."  

Since then, I haven’t reached out to him, nor has he reached out to me. I viewed his walking out as unprofessional, but I’m also wondering if I handled things poorly as a manager or father. AITA for trying to maintain high standards and holding my son accountable like any other employee?

WIBTA if I sold my dead grandmother’s wedding ring? My grandmother passed away last year and she left some of her grandchildren her most expensive jewellery and left me (20, f) her very expensive wedding ring. By expensive i’m talking tens of thousands this ring is worth. 

Personally I don’t see the point in keeping it, I’d rather hold onto the memories of her and the ring would just be sitting in its box on my dresser for the rest of my life. 

I’m a broke university student so in my head it would make sense for me to sell the ring and use it for something that would mean a lot to me. I could use it to a) pay off my student debt b) go travelling or c) use it as saving for a downpayment for a future house. 

To me selling it and using it for that would have much more value and whichever I choose would allow me to remember my grandma how I would personally like to.

My dad told my extended family about me considering selling the ring and they all lost their shit. They genuinely seemed disgusted that I would even consider selling something so valuable to my grandma and grandad (both deceased) and they kept saying its not what she would have wanted me to do with it. Now I do agree that my grandma probably wouldn’t have wanted me to sell it as she was very materialistic and her jewellery meant a lot to her, but she left the ring to me and the ring has little meaning to me. 

Now I am conflicted as I don’t feel anything towards the ring and it wont have any use to me, but I know my grandma wouldn’t have wanted me to sell it.

WITBTA if I sold the ring anyway despite my family’s wishes, knowing that my grandma wouldn’t have wanted me to?

AITA For not wanting to hang with the crew? Throw away because I don’t want my real account found out.  I’ll try and trim all the fat and cut to the chase. This post is strictly “bro code” oriented, so I’m not sure if it’s the right sub but worth a shot. 


- 2 friends and I are out at a nice bar/club. David – who I’m really close with – and John who I met through David. John’s been out with us a few times. I considered John a bro by default, since David’s my bro and has been friends with John for so many years.

- Another friend of David’s, Will, joins us and decides on his own that he wants to buy a bottle for all of us to share out of his own generosity. We have a table exclusive to us thanks to Will. I’ve briefly met Will before, but this is the first time I’ve actually started to get to know him. 

- While away from the table, a blonde girl in a sparkly dress catches my eye. I set on a stool next to where she was sitting, say “Hi, I like your sparkly dress” with a smile. She finishes whatever she was doing on her smart phone, smacks her hand on my shoulder, says “you’re not my type”, briefly using my shoulder as leverage to get up and walk away. EDIT: Let me emphasise this: ***she laid her hands on me in an aggressive manner.*** It wasn't just words. 

- Whatever, I get it. I’ve got a lot of experience approaching girls and never let it phase me. I know that there’s just some girls out there with low self-esteem and need to put down others in order to make themselves feel a semblance of self-adequacy. 

- I return to our table, and it turns out there’s 2 or 3 girls there, talking to Will and David, and also… The sparkly dress girl, who is a friend of those girls. 

- If I chipped in for the bottle/table, I would’ve told the sparkly dress girl that since I’m not her type, she should take a hike, or perhaps call her out and explain how putting other people down isn’t the solution to a low self-esteem. But since Will paid for it all, and was trying to get with one of her friends, I was put in an awkward spot. I was pissed. I told Will & David that she was very rude to me, and asked if I could tell her to fuck off our table. They shrugged their shoulders and didn’t give any clear answer. In hindsight, I wouldn’t have asked. I would’ve just not been at the table and gone solo for the night at the other parts of the bar/club. 

- Anyway, she got up to leave. However, before she left, John started talking to her, so I decided that fuck it, because: 1. A guy who paid for the table is trying to get with her friend and 2. A bro by default is trying to get with the rude girl, I’m just gonna leave and go to another bar that I actually loved going to and know the staff etc. 

- David & John (who I had now explained how rude sparkly dress was to me) insisted I don’t leave, that I shouldn’t let it phase me, etc. I explained that I’m not mad at the girl herself, it’s just the situation that’s fucked. I don’t wanna fuck anyone’s shit up, but I don’t want to hang with that girl as if what she did was acceptable behaviour or not, I’ll just leave and be happy somewhere else. David said to John that he should ditch sparkly dress, but he didn’t. I told John not to, that it's fine, because I believe a friend wouldn't have to be asked to or explained why to not tolerate disrespectful behaviour towards his friend, he just wouldn't.

- I hung around a bit away from the table but eventually left. 

- Lessons learnt from the night: 1) I don’t consider John to be a friend anymore, as he tolerated disrespectful behaviour towards me for the opportunity to get laid and 2) I’m never gonna let anyone buy me anything again, because it creates unwarranted obligations on my behalf. 

Am I the asshole for not wanting to stay at the table and wanting to leave?

AITA for telling my co-worker what to do So this story starts back a year ago, I work for a large mail manufacturer and had been there for 2 years at the time. We hire on just about anyone that can pass a background check. I was made a team lead about a month before the incident and was still very fresh to the role. Before becoming a lead, I was tasked with training the replacement for the machine I was responsible for in order to move on to my new position. The replacement, we’ll call C, was known for being difficult to work with and smelled of alcohol while on the job, my sense of smell has never been great so I could never notice and never became a problem while training him. Well, a month after being a team lead, my boss’s boss tells me that C needs to run a particular job ASAP, that I needed to tell him, and he had no choice in matter due to the urgency of the work (my boss was out for the day). I go to C and tell him exactly that and this came from above me. C gets pissed, goes straight to HR, and then leaves for the day. HR did not send him home, he walked out. The whole dispute get reconciled and I felt shitty for this whole incident, boss’s boss says don’t worry about it, I move on. Zoom forward to a year later, now, I’ve moved on to a new shift, and a new position that has nothing to do with C except lining up the work before his shift starts. I haven’t talk to C in almost the entire time since then, and I have apologized for that time already. Today, I’m running behind in bring the material for the day to the machine C currently runs, I try to help by asking him where he would like the material and if there is anything I can do to help. He turns around and talks quiet enough just for me to hear and clear enough, “I haven’t forgiven you for what you said to me before, and I haven’t forgotten when you told me I didn’t have a choice. I don’t want you talking to me.” I’m not good with confrontation, and I apologized again. But I got no response and I’m feeling worse than when this first happened. AITA?

Despite that, I’ve continued to cook for my family. 

My husband is a little picky with food. Each week I ask him what he’d like. Breakfast, lunch, dinner and snack options. I ask him weekly because he complains that there’s nothing he wants to eat. I ask him at those times what he’d like (so I can stick it on the list) but he says he never knows - unless it’s fast food.

I just want to add that I am a good cook- everyone likes my food, my husband has invited people for dinner before to ‘show off’ my cooking and I’m often asked for my recipes or food requests are made of me. AITA for defending my elderly dog at the dog park? I was at the dog park with my elderly, small-ish dog (about 20 lbs). Even though there is a small dog area, my dog usually enjoys the large dog section because he likes exploring in bigger spaces, and he's always done fine in the past. While we were there, my spouse and I ended up chatting with a young woman and her friend, who had their dogs with them. The conversation was pleasant enough, but shortly after we parted ways, one of their dogs—a larger, rambunctious one—ran full speed into my dog, knocking him over. 

When the dog collided with my elderly dog, I was upset and worried about my dog's safety, so my initial reaction was to swat at the larger dog and yell to scare it off. We’ve been together five years, lived together for three. When we met we had a number of shared interests as well as our own separate things. She had DnD which I’ve never been interested in, while I had local sports and classic literature which she couldn’t care less about.

Over time that changed. She started coming with me to see live sport. She would ask me about the books I was reading. Within a year or so we would go to every event together and her collection of jerseys matched mine, and she would read any book I recommend and dissect it with me. It was wonderful. Both of us have always been solitary types, I’ve always pursued my hobbies alone and now I was able to share them with someone. And with the person I loved too!

Over time that has changed. My girlfriend is far better at communicating with people than I am (thank you, sheltered religious upbringing and neurodiversity) and she started ingratiating herself into communities around our interests. She started contributing to local sports discussions and finding herself invited to social events, meeting the athletes, volunteering for community groups. Book discussions spilled into online communities, which became visiting signings and podcasts.

Today she chairs the official fans’ trust of our local soccer team, and was granted access by the estate of my favourite author to go through his notes for the purposes of a documentary about him. I hate it. I hate all the busy-ness, all the people and back-patting and schmoozing. I don’t even want to go back to being just me and her going to games, discussing books until one in the morning. I just want to enjoy my hobbies by myself again.

I’ve looked within over and over to try and work out why I feel this way. I’ve never been a gatekeeper, I only ever want to open doors and encourage people. I don’t think I’m a misogynist or a fragile man who resents successful women. My exes include a very influential businesswoman and professional gymnast while I’ve always had a boring mid-level office job, never had any problems with jealousy or resentment there. And yet I do find myself feeling jealous and resentful of my girlfriend. Perhaps it’s because these are “my” interests and I feel incapable of making any of the social strides she’s made. Perhaps I’ve made the “lone wolf” element of my fandom into more of my identity than I realised to compensate for that.

These are new feelings for me, they’ve crept up on me and I have no idea what to do about it. I feel especially guilty because I haven’t talked to her about it. We have always been able to have difficult conversations and understand that they need to happen sometimes. Yet I feel paralysed and unable to discuss this with her.

At the end of the year we’re going abroad for a convention about one of my favourite film series. I just want to mill around at my own pace, take it all in… and I just know that she’s going to schmooze her way into charming the actors and filmmakers I adore in a way that I simply cannot. Honestly, I wish I were going by myself and I feel terrible for that.

I don’t know where to begin working any of this out and I feel so guilty for feeling this way. My girlfriend is a wonderful woman who has continued to adore me the entire time we’re together and would probably sacrifice all of her accomplishments to stay with me. I don’t feel worthy of that.

**TL;DR: My girlfriend has slowly become an influential figure in the arenas around my hobbies. I am feeling resentful of this for reasons I am not sure of and wish I could go back to simpler times when it was just me and my interests.**
